data.narrative:
Insitro, a Series C-stage biotech company founded by Daphne Koller, has raised $1.1B+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 3 public peers (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers in the Biotech & Health sector, including same-stage comparables Colossal Biosciences ($10.3B), Chai Discovery ($3.8B), and New Limit ($3.1B).

Two valuation methods proved applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement to the $1.1B total raised proxy, implying $1.9B. Peer-median anchoring across the three same-sector, same-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $3.8B, with a range spanning $3.1B to $10.3B. Public-comp P/S anchoring, while available at 8.1x median across the three public tickers, cannot be applied absent disclosed revenue for the target company.

The triangulated analysis across these two applicable methods supports a valuation range of $1.6B (low) to $4.4B (high), with a median of $2.8B. Key uncertainties include the wide dispersion within the peer set—driven primarily by Colossal Biosciences' $10.3B valuation—and the absence of revenue data, which limits validation via public market multiples. Stage timing and capital efficiency relative to peers remain material variables.
